title: Songs by the River
paragraphs: Then came the worst thing of all. Enemy armies took the city, and many people were marched far away to Babylon. They sat by a river and could hardly sing. "How can we sing Yahweh's song in a foreign land?" they asked. They missed their home, their temple, their friends. But God sent a message through Jeremiah: settle down, plant gardens, and pray for the place you live in. God had not forgotten them. He would bring them back and give them hope and a future. And a new promise: a time when God's law would be written not on stone but on their hearts. Even in exile, God was planning a way home.
wonder: I wonder what keeps hope alive when you are far from home?
prayer: God of the far-away and the homesick, hold those who are lost or lonely and bring them home. Amen.
alt: Harps hang from willow trees beside a river at dusk, with a golden thread crossing to the far bank.
translation: Retold in our own words, with short quotations from the World English Bible.
